dish.title: Pakistani Chicken Karahi with Warm Naan
dish.description: Bone-in chicken seared hard in a wok-shaped karahi or wide skillet, then cooked down with fresh tomatoes, plenty of ginger, garlic, and green chiles until the sauce clings and the oil separates. Finished with julienned ginger and cilantro and served with warm naan.

recipe_version.title: Pakistani Chicken Karahi with Warm Naan
recipe_version.description: Bone-in chicken seared hard in a wok-shaped karahi or wide skillet, then cooked down with fresh tomatoes, plenty of ginger, garlic, and green chiles until the sauce clings and the oil separates. Finished with julienned ginger and cilantro and served with warm naan.

ingredients.name: bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
ingredients.note: thighs cut in half through the bone by the butcher, or left whole

ingredients.name: fresh ginger
ingredients.note: 3 inches grated, 1 inch julienned for garnish

ingredients.name: naan
ingredients.display_name: plain naan whose label lists wheat flour, milk or yogurt, oil, and leavening, with no egg, soy, or sesame

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Pat the chicken dry. Chop the tomatoes. Grate 3 inches of the ginger and julienne the last inch. Grate the garlic. Chop 2 chiles and slit the other 2. Chop the cilantro, cut the lemon into wedges, and thinly slice the red onion.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.body: Heat the oil in a 12-inch wok or deep skillet over high until shimmering. Add the chicken skin side down with the cumin seeds and sear, turning, until browned all over, about 8 minutes.

steps.title: Add the aromatics
steps.body: Add the grated ginger, garlic, and chopped chiles and stir 1 minute.

steps.title: Cook down the tomatoes
steps.body: Add the tomatoes, salt, chile flakes, coriander, and black pepper. Cook over medium-high, stirring and turning the chicken often, until the tomatoes collapse and the sauce thickens, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Finish the karahi
steps.body: Cover and cook over medium-low until the chicken reads 175 F at the bone, about 12 minutes, stirring once. Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high, and stir until the sauce clings and oil separates at the edges, about 4 minutes. Stir in the garam masala and slit chiles.

steps.title: Warm the naan
steps.body: While the karahi finishes uncovered, wrap the naan in foil and warm it on a sheet pan set on the back of the stove, or one at a time in a dry skillet over medium, about 1 minute each (overlap stated).

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Scatter the julienned ginger and cilantro over the karahi and serve from the pan with lemon wedges, the sliced red onion, and the warm naan.

equipment: 12-inch wok, karahi, or deep skillet with lid
sheet pan or foil for warming naan

coverage_contribution: First Pakistani meal. A dry, tomato-led chicken curry unlike butter chicken (creamy) or adobo (vinegar). Weeknight wok cooking.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with pressure-cooker-butter-chicken: no cream or butter, cooked fast at high heat until dry and clinging; bone-in. Compared with filipino-chicken-adobo: tomato-ginger-chile, not vinegar-soy. Compared with hungarian-chicken-paprikash: no sour cream or paprika gravy; served with naan.
not_duplicate_of: Not chicken tikka masala (a creamy tomato curry would echo butter chicken).
